headline: EnEarth acquires Storegga's 30% stake and Lead Developer role in Acorn CCS
summary: EnEarth, the carbon-storage arm spun out of Energean, has signed a sale-and-purchase agreement to take Storegga's 30% working interest and Lead Developer role in the Acorn CO2 transport-and-storage project in north-east Scotland, folding Acorn into a planned pan-European CO2 storage platform.
co2crc_note: Developer consolidation at a flagship UK Track-2 cluster; a Mediterranean CO2-storage player building a pan-European T&S platform shows how CCS operatorship is consolidating across borders.
extractor_note: Deal value not disclosed. Page date not WebFetch-verified (hosts blocked); 23 Nov confirmed via Google Alerts timestamps and multiple corroborating Tier-1/2 search sources.

headline: Study argues a 'Carbon Takeback' obligation on North Sea producers could fund first wave of UK CCS
summary: BusinessGreen reports on research arguing that a Carbon Takeback Obligation - requiring oil and gas producers to store a rising share of the CO2 embedded in their products - could fund the first wave of UK CCS without relying on open-ended taxpayer subsidy.
co2crc_note: Carbon takeback / producer-pays mechanisms are a live alternative to grant-funded CCS and directly relevant to how Australia might finance storage without perpetual subsidy.
extractor_note: Reports on a policy study/proposal (no money committed). Underlying carbon-takeback research predates the window (earlier Oxford/Green Alliance work); treated as fresh on BusinessGreen's 23 Nov news framing. Page date not WebFetch-verified; from Google Alerts metadata.

headline: CNPC's Xinjiang oilfield CCUS project passes 2 million tonnes cumulative CO2 injection
summary: PetroChina/CNPC reported that cumulative CO2 injection at its Xinjiang oilfield CCUS-EOR project in north-west China has passed 2 million tonnes, with plans for a CO2 pipeline network during the 15th Five-Year Plan to replace tanker-truck transport.
co2crc_note: Illustrates steady Chinese NOC CCUS-EOR build-out; a reference point for commercial injection scale-up in a systematically under-covered region.
extractor_note: Radar item: published 17 Nov, outside the 23-24 Nov window but within 7 days. Cumulative injection figure is a resource/cumulative total, not an annual capacity - capacity_mtpa left null (non-additive).
